lessons.title: Words the C64 has already claimed

exercises.title: Type and predict
exercises.text: Put the number of levels you've beaten in one variable and the number still to go in another. Before printing their sum, write down what it will be.

exercises.title: Fix it
exercises.text: These commands don't work. Find both problems, explain each in one sentence, and fix them: SCORE = 40, then TOTAL = SCORE + 10.

exercises.title: Build it
exercises.text: Use three variables: your name, a reward you'd like to earn, and how many points it costs. Make the C64 print one sentence about it. Add all three to your variable dictionary first, with their data types.

quiz.question: After C = 6 and then C = C * 3, what does PRINT C show?
After P% = 5.7, what does PRINT P% show?
Which variable can hold the word GEMS?
Which of these names is always safe?
A program uses DAMAGE and DASH. What goes wrong?

lessons.title: Fixing a line on the screen

exercises.title: Predict the order
exercises.text: Type NEW, then these lines in this order: 40 PRINT "FOUR", 20 PRINT "TWO", 10 PRINT "ONE", 30 PRINT "THREE". Before typing LIST and RUN, write down what each will show.

exercises.title: Fix it two ways
exercises.text: Type the HIGH SCORE program from Lesson 2.4. Fix line 20 once by retyping the whole line, then break it again and fix it with the screen editor. Which way was faster?

exercises.title: Build it
exercises.text: Plan a program on paper that shows three of your best scores or achievements, one per line, using variables from your variable dictionary. Number the lines by tens, type it, and run it. Then add a title line at the top *without* retyping anything else.

quiz.question: You type 10 PRINT "GO!" and press RETURN. What happens?

options.text: The line is stored and nothing is printed

quiz.question: You type lines 50, then 20, then 40. What does LIST show first?
What does typing 40 by itself and pressing RETURN do?

options.text: It leaves room to add lines in between

quiz.question: Which command erases the whole program?
